source: Six learner attempts saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Dime si reporting requests and keeping meaning in longer instructions
summary: Correctly used feminine read/review sequence. Introduced Dime si... with unaccented whether-si. Readiness extension correct. Grammatical Dime si lo publicamos differed from requested can-publish meaning; after correction, can-test and need-review requests correct. Final sequence retained reporting clause and agreement but omitted explicit it from first review command; revísala supplied.

observations.outcome: Correct order and feminine object-command forms after prior models; accents supplied. Tutor then introduced Dime si está lista, translating dime si as tell me whether and noting unaccented si.

observations.learnerText: Dime si el logo esta listo
observations.correctedText: Dime si el logo está listo.
observations.outcome: Correct extension of modelled dime si with explicit noun subject and masculine readiness agreement. Está accent supplied.

Grammatical Tell me whether we're publishing it, with valid lo placement. Prompt asked whether we can publish it; missing ability meaning supplied as Dime si lo podemos publicar / Dime si podemos publicarlo. Do not mark publicamos itself ungrammatical or count as successful can-publish production.
Correct podemos + infinitive with attached masculine lo after ability correction; no full test-it target model supplied.
Correct transfer to necesitamos + feminine revisarla without a fresh full model.

observations.learnerText: primero revisa, luego dime si esta lista
observations.correctedText: Primero revísala; luego dime si está lista.
observations.outcome: Correct sequence, command revisa and dime si readiness clause with feminine lista. First command omitted explicit requested it; tutor supplied revísala. Raw shorter revisa is understandable in context and not treated as wholly ungrammatical. Está accent supplied.

nextSteps: Keep explicit objects in multi-step commands
Preserve can versus simple present meaning
Recheck prueba stem after this intervening topic
assessmentNote: Different grammatical meanings are acknowledged rather than scored as universally wrong. Prompted immediate transfers and supplied accents do not establish long-term retention.
